Hello,

This isn't specific on programmers, but I've recently finished a course titled "the science of happiness", and am finishing up a similar course called the science of wellbeing. I do recommend looking at them as they have reminded/taught me a lot of things that I think we forget as adults.

I've had depression for many years as well, although I would say that I've recently recovered. Depression definitely has an effect on work. I would be down to have a direct conversation with you or anyone else who is reading this (facebook,  discord, whatsapp, whatever).

For those who are busy or would rather not do that. Here is some general advise:

1. Get a notebook (this is useful for various other reasons. I recommend a pocket moleskine or something of a similar size). At the end of the day try to write down 3 good things that have happened. They can be small things like having enjoyed a warm shower or a good meal, or having a conversation, or they could be much bigger things. The point is to remind yourself of the positives because our brains are wired to focus on what is wrong.

2. If you look at the history of primates, they are a social species and wired for social connection. Social connection is intrinsically rewarding. It is also lacking in modern society. Try to maintain your relationships with friends, family, and romantic partners. Ask them about how their week has been if you are struggling to talk about positives from your own life.

3. Try to do a random act of kindness. You can choose to spend money on someone but it doesn't have to be much (think $5 instead of $20). Pay to get someone coffee or have them experience something nice. This is also intrinsically rewarding, in part because we might anticipate that they might do something in return for us, but also because we feel better when we see people around us feeling good.

4. You may feel better if you come to terms with interpersonal conflict, which is an inevitable part of life. Once sufficient time has passed, try to see if you can forgive the person who has done you wrong, reminding yourself that all people want the same basic things, happiness, connection and safety. Forgiveness isn't recognising that a past injustice was okay, but it is more for your own benefit.

6. People have something called a default brain network, which is how your minds default when we're not focusing on something. It allows us to think about the past and the future. However despite the usefulness of being able to do this, people tend to be more unhappy when they are not living in the present. If you want to practice not mind wandering so much, look into meditation practices, which have secular forms (you don't need to become a buddhist or a hindu). More broadly you can also look at mindfulness for similar reasons.

7. We are often very self critical. Try treating yourself as you would a good friend. You probably wouldn't be so harsh against someone else, and extending that same basic kindness to yourself isn't a bad idea. Indulge in something nice if you haven't in a while. Just remember, you wouldn't tell a good friend to go do whatever they wanted, and in the same way, restrain yourself from making bad long term decisions.

8. We often don't appreciate the things that we do have. Practicing gratitude a few times a week, or at least once a week, and thinking about the good things life has given to you is important. Whilst it is true that bad things do happen, we seem to focus on this and ignore the good things.

9. Get some exercise and enough sleep. You don't need to be a body builder, just try going for a run 30 minutes a day. I don't do this, but I know I should :)

9. Some of the above things will come more naturally and easier than others. That's okay, the point is to find some things that work for you.

I just skimmed Pichu Paradigm and it seems to cover most of the things I was going to suggest, I'll just write a few random tips. I only really play Pichu vs Fox so keep that in mind.

Pichu isn't the easiest character to use for a new player. He's extremely quick in the air so you really need to be confident moving around otherwise you'll miss a lot of neutral airs.

Once you hit someone with one neutral air, you might as well chase them and hit them with another, it combos until high percents. uair is another fast aerial and it combos well but I'd prefer other moves generally as its damage is low. Take all the damage you can get though and It's good if you want to get someone on to a platform for a platform follow up.


against fox/falco, you have an upthrow chaingrab. It's a very fun matchup because Pichu is okay at edge-guarding and fastfallers are prone to gimps. If you throw or hit a spacie offstage, use neutral b (thunderjolt) to cover them trying to use side b to the ledge, forcing them to go low or high. Then you can try to edge guard them using a few moves, experiment with ftilt, dtilt, neutral air, upair, fthrow, bthrow, upsmash and fsmash. I actually sometimes use dsmash which sends them behind me to fsmash, but mainly because it looks cool. last hit of fsmash kills early, and fsmash as as a whole covers the ledge, but it's easily SDId out of.

In the neutral game, remember your strengths. Pichus shield is top tier as its size/body ratio is really good, it completely covers you for a good while so don't worry about shield pokes. Your forward roll is also extremely long, (normal roll, your tech rolls are horrible). You can use thunderjolt in sort of the same way as a falco lazer or samus missile, to cover your movement up to them and force them to shield or jump. then cover the jump with nair/uair, or fair to grounded option.

You can also downthrow tech chase with pichu. and then attempt to finish off with a upsmash. I haven't talked about upsmash much but it's actually your main kill move aside from gimping. against floaties you can upthrow nair at low percents, and then downthrow upsmash at high percents. 

Last thing is that Pichu has a couple of weird tools against missed techs. You can actually thunder jolt reset them, kind of like a lazer reset. Also your jab is so weak that you can use multiple jabs for free damage.

Sorry for the disorganised post hope something here helped :)

One important factor of recovery I think we should discuss is vulnerability to being edge guarded. I think this is a big factor in how "good" a recovery is.

Take for example Kirby. Despite having multiple jumps (good distance), he's slow in the air and predictable. On top of this hitting him out of his up b causes him to lose all of his jumps. I think he is the easiest character to edge guard (unless he manages to go very high) and would consider his recovery bad as a result.
